# Cost and Performance

Developer experience impact, overhead, and workflow disruption.

## Permission Prompt Reduction

The headline metric: sandbox auto-allow mode reduces permission prompts
by **84%** in Anthropic's internal usage [2].

One user reported daily prompts dropping from **~200+ to 5-10** with
sandbox auto-allow enabled [19].

This addresses **approval fatigue** — "Repeatedly clicking 'approve' can
cause users to pay less attention to what they're approving" [1]. The Ona
research demonstrated this concretely: an agent's request to disable the
sandbox was "one more 'yes' in a stream of 'yes'" [6].

## Sandbox Performance Overhead

| Metric | Value | Source |
|--------|-------|--------|
| Fixed overhead per sandboxed call | ~80-160ms | [11] |
| Steady-state (proxies persist) | "tens of milliseconds" | [11] |
| Official characterization | "Minimal" | [1] |

"Only noticeable in scripts spawning hundreds of tiny bash calls" [11].
Commands doing real work pay the overhead once, then run at full speed [11].

## Hook Performance

| Metric | Value |
|--------|-------|
| Command/HTTP hook timeout | 30s default [14] |
| Agent hook timeout | 60s default [14] |
| Async hooks | Non-blocking [3] |

Hooks add latency per tool call — each PreToolUse hook runs serially
before execution [3]. For simple pattern-matching scripts, this is
sub-second. For complex validation (LLM prompt hooks, agent hooks),
it can be seconds.

## Tool Compatibility Issues

These tools are documented as broken or requiring workarounds with
sandbox enabled:

| Tool | Issue | Workaround |
|------|-------|------------|
| Docker | Incompatible with sandbox | `excludedCommands: ["docker *"]` [1] |
| watchman | Incompatible | `jest --no-watchman` [1] |
| Go CLI (macOS) | Temp directory access denied [18] | No workaround [18] |
| Git init/clone | Hardcoded .git/* denials [11] | — |
| Node native fetch | Ignores proxy, bypasses network isolation [11] | — |
| gh CLI | TLS cert verification fails [11] | — |
| WSL1 | No kernel namespace support | Upgrade to WSL2 [1] |

## Setup Complexity

**Sandbox setup:** run `/sandbox`, choose mode, approve domain requests
as they arise. Configuration converges over a few sessions [1].

**Hooks setup:** write validation scripts, configure matchers, test exit
code behavior, deploy to settings.json. Trail of Bits provides starter
configs [8].

**Combined setup guidance** from enterprise rollout guide [26]:
- Day 1 (30 min): block destructive commands via PreToolUse hook
- Week 1 (2 hrs): add PostToolUse security scanning
- Production ready (half day): audit logging, input sanitization

## Developer Experience Trade-offs

### Sandbox Benefits
- Fewer interruptions → deeper focus
- Agent works more autonomously within boundaries
- Security enforced without constant vigilance

### Sandbox Friction
- Tool incompatibilities require `excludedCommands` per tool
- Default read access too broad — requires manual denyRead config [11]
- Go/Docker development may be impractical without escape hatches [18]
- Overly restrictive policies break production within 48 hours [24]

### Hooks Benefits
- Deterministic enforcement: "A prompt instruction achieves 90%
  compliance. A hook achieves 100%" [27]
- Semantic validation (intent-based, not just pattern-based) [8]
- Audit trail of every tool call [3]

### Hooks Friction
- Every hook adds latency to tool calls
- Exit code semantics confusing (1=non-blocking, 2=blocking) [3]
- Must maintain hook scripts as project evolves
- No visual feedback during hook execution unless statusMessage set [3]

## Cost Comparison

| Aspect | Sandbox | Hooks | Both |
|--------|---------|-------|------|
| Setup time | ~5 min | ~30 min to 1 day | ~1 day |
| Ongoing maintenance | Low (config) | Medium (scripts) | Medium |
| Tool breakage risk | Medium-High | None | Medium-High |
| Permission prompt reduction | 84% [2] | Depends on logic | 84%+ |
| Security coverage | Bash only | All tools | All tools + OS Bash |

## Gaps and Limitations

- No published benchmarks comparing sandbox overhead on macOS (Seatbelt)
  vs Linux (bubblewrap) [11]
- Performance data from a single third-party source (claudecodecamp.com)
- Hook latency not quantified in official documentation
- No A/B comparison of developer productivity with vs without sandbox
- Enterprise deployment cost (time to configure for team) undocumented
